sections.content:
Two parties hold sets \(X\) and \(Y\) and want \(X\cap Y\) without revealing
anything about the items outside it (PSI-PAPER-2018-PSZ). Usually one party,
the receiver, learns the intersection and the other, the sender, learns
nothing; the set sizes are typically public. With more parties, all of them
compute the intersection of their sets and learn nothing else beyond bounds on
the set sizes (PSI-PAPER-2018-EKR). Variants release only a function of the
intersection: its size, a sum of values attached to its items, a decision on
whether it is large, or secret shares for a further secure computation. Generic
secure computation can compute PSI, and garbled-circuit PSI ran as fast as the
public-key protocols of its time, or faster at higher security levels, at much
higher bandwidth (PSI-PAPER-2012-HEK); protocols that exploit the structure of
the problem are more efficient (PSI-PAPER-2018-EKR). Applications include
private contact discovery from a phone (PSI-PAPER-2017-CLR,
PSI-PAPER-2019-KRSSW) and aggregate ad-conversion statistics
(PSI-PAPER-2020-ION).
sections.heading: What it is

sections.content:
- **Adversaries**: semi-honest parties follow the protocol; augmented
  semi-honest parties may change their inputs and then follow it
  (PSI-PAPER-2017-KMPRT); malicious parties deviate arbitrarily. Security can
  differ by party, as in protocols that are simulation-secure against a
  malicious receiver but only private against a malicious sender
  (PSI-PAPER-2018-CHLR).
- **Set-size slack**: the fastest malicious protocols realize a relaxed
  functionality in which a corrupt party may effectively input more items than
  it declared, up to a constant factor (PSI-PAPER-2017-RR-CCS,
  PSI-PAPER-2020-PRTY, PSI-PAPER-2021-RT).
- **Balanced and unbalanced**: sets of similar size, or a small receiver set
  against a much larger sender set, where communication can be sublinear in
  the larger set (PSI-PAPER-2017-CLR).
- **Outputs**: the intersection; its cardinality; an intersection-sum, the sum
  of values attached to matching items (PSI-PAPER-2020-ION); threshold PSI,
  which releases the intersection only when the sets differ in few items
  (PSI-PAPER-2019-GS); circuit-PSI, secret shares of per-item results that feed
  a further secure computation (PSI-PAPER-2018-PSWW, PSI-PAPER-2019-PSTY); and
  labeled PSI, which returns labels the sender attaches to matching items
  (PSI-PAPER-2018-CHLR).
- **Hashing to bins**: items are mapped into bins by simple hashing or by
  cuckoo hashing, which places each item in one of a few candidate bins,
  possibly with a stash, so that per-bin work is small; parameters are set
  for a hashing failure probability such as \(2^{-40}\) (PSI-PAPER-2018-PSZ).
- **Oblivious PRF (OPRF)**: the receiver learns \(F_k(y)\) for its items while
  the sender holds \(k\) and sends \(F_k(x)\) for its own items, so the
  receiver compares values (PSI-PAPER-2018-EKR); many instances can be
  produced at once from OT extension (PSI-PAPER-2016-KKRT).
- **Oblivious key-value store (OKVS)**: a data structure that encodes
  key-value pairs and hides the keys when the values are random; a polynomial
  through the pairs is the simplest one (PSI-PAPER-2021-GPRTY), and PaXoS is a
  binary one decoded by XOR (PSI-PAPER-2020-PRTY).
- **Lower bounds**: computing the intersection needs communication linear in
  the set size, by the complexity of disjointness (PSI-PAPER-2004-FNP;
  PSI-PAPER-2019-GS); threshold PSI needs \(\Omega(t)\) for two parties
  (PSI-PAPER-2019-GS) and \(\Omega(\ell t)\) for \(\ell\) parties over
  point-to-point channels (PSI-PAPER-2021-BMRR); and PSI implies oblivious
  transfer, so it has no black-box construction from one-way functions
  (PSI-PAPER-2004-FNP).
sections.heading: Core notions

sections.content:
- **Public-key-based**: commutative Diffie-Hellman exponentiation of hashed
  items (PSI-PAPER-1999-HFH), oblivious polynomial evaluation under additively
  homomorphic encryption (PSI-PAPER-2004-FNP), RSA blind signatures as the
  OPRF (PSI-PAPER-2010-DT), and PSI from any two-round key agreement with
  responses encoded in a polynomial, which suits small sets
  (PSI-PAPER-2021-RT).
- **OT- and VOLE-based**: OPRFs from OT extension combined with hashing to
  bins (PSI-PAPER-2018-PSZ, PSI-PAPER-2016-KKRT); malicious security by dual
  execution (PSI-PAPER-2017-RR-CCS) and by encoding the receiver's set in a
  PaXoS, with linear communication (PSI-PAPER-2020-PRTY); general OKVS and
  amplification of their failure probability (PSI-PAPER-2021-GPRTY); OPRFs
  from vector oblivious linear evaluation (VOLE) (PSI-PAPER-2021-RS); and
  subfield VOLE with a triangulation OKVS (PSI-PAPER-2022-RR).
- **Circuit-based and computing on the intersection**: a sort-compare-shuffle
  garbled circuit (PSI-PAPER-2012-HEK); hashing-based circuits with
  \(\omega(n)\) comparisons (PSI-PAPER-2018-PSWW) and with \(O(n)\)
  communication through batched oblivious programmable PRFs (OPPRF)
  (PSI-PAPER-2019-PSTY, PSI-PAPER-2021-RS); intersection-sum with cardinality
  from Diffie-Hellman double masking (PSI-PAPER-2020-ION); and threshold PSI
  from polynomial encodings and cardinality tests (PSI-PAPER-2019-GS,
  PSI-PAPER-2021-BMRR, PSI-PAPER-2023-GS).
- **Unbalanced and labeled**: fully homomorphic encryption with batching, so
  that the sender evaluates the intersection on the receiver's encrypted set
  (PSI-PAPER-2017-CLR), with OPRF preprocessing and labels
  (PSI-PAPER-2018-CHLR) and lower computation and communication
  (PSI-PAPER-2021-CONG); alternatively the server's OPRF-encrypted set is
  transferred once and queried online (PSI-PAPER-2019-KRSSW).
- **Multiparty**: zero-sharing delivered through OPPRFs, secure against any
  number of colluding semi-honest parties (PSI-PAPER-2017-KMPRT), malicious
  versions over OKVS (PSI-PAPER-2021-GPRTY, PSI-PAPER-2021-NTY), and protocols
  from homomorphic set representations surveyed in PSI-PAPER-2024-VCE.

Costs in the comparison tables are recorded per role, as the papers state
them: what each role sends and the work it performs. A figure a paper states
only for the whole protocol is recorded as the total; it is never split among
the roles, and role figures are never summed into one.

| Role | Meaning | Regime | Paper names |

| Sender | Holds the set \(X\), of size \(n_X\); in one-sided PSI, the party that does not learn the output. | Two-party PSI. | PSI-PAPER-1999-HFH writes "Alice"; PSI-PAPER-2004-FNP writes "server"; PSI-PAPER-2010-DT writes "server"; PSI-PAPER-2019-KRSSW writes "server"; PSI-PAPER-2020-ION writes "P1"; PSI-PAPER-2019-GS writes "Bob" |
