sections.heading: Notation

sections.content:
This topic covers two-party and multiparty PSI and functions of the
intersection (cardinality, intersection-sum, threshold, circuit outputs,
labels) in five subfields: public-key-based, OT- and VOLE-based,
circuit-based, unbalanced and labeled, and multiparty PSI. Server-aided and
delegated PSI, fuzzy and updatable PSI, private set union, and PSI from trusted
hardware are outside it; OT extension, VOLE, and garbling belong to secure
multiparty computation, and keyword PIR to private information retrieval. The
covered papers date from 1999 to 2024; later work, including maliciously
secure circuit-PSI, is not yet covered.
sections.heading: Scope of this atlas

primer.summary: Protocols that let parties holding private sets learn the intersection of those sets, or a function of it, without revealing anything else about the items outside it.
primer.title: Private set intersection

lanes.label: Foundation
lanes.question: What is the problem, and what can be established or ruled out?

lanes.label: Efficiency
lanes.question: Which resource cost or trade-off is advanced?

PSI-CONTRIB-1999-HFH-DH-PREFERENCE-MATCH.label: Diffie-Hellman preference matching
PSI-CONTRIB-1999-HFH-DH-PREFERENCE-MATCH.lane_rationale: The principal claim is a concrete protocol, commutative exponentiation of hashed items, that realizes private matching without a trusted third party; no cost or bound is claimed.
PSI-CONTRIB-1999-HFH-DH-PREFERENCE-MATCH.selection_rationale: The protocol that later papers call the classic Diffie-Hellman PSI (PSI-PAPER-2021-RT §1, p. 1); recorded as the paper states it, a matching count with a variation that reveals the shared items (Appendix A, p. 85).

PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-APPROX-LOWER-BOUND.label: Lower bound for approximate intersection size
PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-APPROX-LOWER-BOUND.lane_rationale: A communication lower bound; the rubric routes lower bounds to Foundation.
PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-APPROX-LOWER-BOUND.selection_rationale: Shows by reduction from disjointness that multiplicative approximation of intersection size needs linear communication (§6, pp. 13-14), ruling out sublinear private approximation.
PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-APPROX-LOWER-BOUND.split_rationale: Belongs to the line of communication lower bounds, separate from the paper's polynomial-evaluation protocols: Ghosh and Simkin turn this disjointness-based bound into the \( \Omega(t) \) bound for threshold PSI (PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-LOWER-BOUND).

PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-OPE-PSI.label: Polynomial-evaluation PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-OPE-PSI.lane_rationale: A new reusable method, set encoding as polynomial roots evaluated under homomorphic encryption, answering how PSI is realized in the standard model.
PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-OPE-PSI.selection_rationale: Root of the map: the paper formulates private matching, two-party set intersection, with cardinality and threshold variants (§3.1, p. 3) and semi-honest and malicious adversary models (§3.2, p. 4), and this protocol realizes it from oblivious polynomial evaluation with standard-model semi-honest security (abstract, p. 1; Protocol PM-Semi-Honest, p. 6); the paper's malicious and multiparty protocols build on it.

PSI-CONTRIB-2012-HEK-SORT-COMPARE-SHUFFL.label: Sort-compare-shuffle PSI circuit
PSI-CONTRIB-2012-HEK-SORT-COMPARE-SHUFFL.lane_rationale: The principal delta is a reusable circuit design (merge, filter, shuffle) that realizes PSI with generic secure computation; its \( \Theta(n \log n) \) size follows from the design, so the rubric routes it to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2012-HEK-SORT-COMPARE-SHUFFL.selection_rationale: The quasi-linear generic PSI circuit (Table 1, p. 2; §5, pp. 5-10) that later circuit-PSI papers use as their baseline (PSI-PAPER-2018-PSWW §6.2; PSI-PAPER-2019-PSTY Table 3).

PSI-CONTRIB-2016-KKRT-BATCHED-OPRF.label: Batched related-key OPRF
PSI-CONTRIB-2016-KKRT-BATCHED-OPRF.lane_rationale: The principal delta is a reusable mechanism, a batched related-key OPRF obtained by using a pseudorandom code in OT extension; the lower cost per instance follows from it, so the rubric routes it to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2016-KKRT-BATCHED-OPRF.selection_rationale: Introduces a batched OPRF from OT extension whose OT cost per instance does not depend on input length (abstract, p. 1; §5.3, p. 12); the PSI protocol of the same paper uses it in place of the earlier byte-wise OPRF.

PSI-CONTRIB-2017-CLR-FHE-SUBLINEAR-COMMU.label: FHE-based PSI, communication logarithmic in the larger set
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-CLR-FHE-SUBLINEAR-COMMU.lane_rationale: The principal delta is a way to realize PSI, homomorphic evaluation of each bin's root polynomial on the receiver's batched ciphertexts, which the later FHE-based unbalanced line reuses; the communication bound follows from this mechanism, so the rubric routes it to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-CLR-FHE-SUBLINEAR-COMMU.selection_rationale: The paper presents it as the first secure and practical PSI with low communication overhead from leveled FHE, linear in the smaller set and logarithmic in the larger one (CLR17 §1.4, p. 3; p. 4); CHLR18 and CMGD21 build directly on its framework (CHLR18 §2, pp. 6-7; CMGD21 §3, p. 5).

PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-OPPRF.label: Oblivious programmable PRF
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-OPPRF.lane_rationale: A reusable mechanism, an OPRF whose outputs the sender can program on chosen points without the receiver noticing; the paper presents it as a new notion with three constructions.
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-OPPRF.selection_rationale: The abstract calls it the technical core and of independent interest (p. 1); NTY reuse its definitions almost verbatim and run OPPRFs inside ZeroXOR (NTY §2, p. 4; Protocol 4.2, p. 10).
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-OPPRF.split_rationale: Belongs to the OPPRF line, which it starts, separate from the multiparty protocol of PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-SYMMETRIC-KEY-MPSI: the batched OPPRF of PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-BATCHED-OPPRF adapts it, and Nevo, Trieu, and Yanai take its definitions almost verbatim and run OPPRFs inside ZeroXOR (PSI-CONTRIB-2021-NTY-MALICIOUS-THRESHOLD-CALIBRATED).

PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-SYMMETRIC-KEY-MPS.label: Multiparty PSI from OPPRF zero-sharing
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-SYMMETRIC-KEY-MPS.lane_rationale: The principal claim is a concrete multiparty protocol, conditional zero-sharing and reconstruction over OPPRFs, that realizes PSI against any number of colluding semi-honest parties; its cost profile follows from that design.
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-SYMMETRIC-KEY-MPS.selection_rationale: The authors call it the first implemented multiparty PSI protocol (abstract, p. 1), and its public-key operations do not depend on the set size, unlike the earlier protocols of Table 1 (p. 3).

PSI-CONTRIB-2017-RR-CCS-MALICIOUS-DUAL-E.label: Dual-execution malicious PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-RR-CCS-MALICIOUS-DUAL-E.lane_rationale: A stronger-secure protocol built on a reusable mechanism, dual execution of oblivious encodings; the rubric routes hardened protocols and mechanisms to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2017-RR-CCS-MALICIOUS-DUAL-E.selection_rationale: Gives the first fully malicious protocol in the OT-based paradigm of Pinkas, Schneider, and Zohner, as the paper states (§1.2, p. 3; Theorem 2, p. 13), with a standard-model instantiation.

PSI-CONTRIB-2018-CHLR-LABELED-PSI.label: Labeled PSI sublinear in the sender's set
PSI-CONTRIB-2018-CHLR-LABELED-PSI.lane_rationale: Realizes a functionality, labeled PSI with communication sublinear in the sender's set, by a concrete mechanism (label-interpolation polynomials); Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2018-CHLR-LABELED-PSI.selection_rationale: Title-level contribution; the paper states that earlier label-returning PSI protocols are linear in the larger set (§1.3, p. 3) and relates the result to single-server keyword PIR (§1.5, p. 5); CMGD21 builds its labeled mode on it (CMGD21 §4, pp. 12-14).

PSI-CONTRIB-2018-PSWW-2D-CUCKOO-HASHING.label: Two-dimensional cuckoo hashing for circuit-PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2018-PSWW-2D-CUCKOO-HASHING.lane_rationale: A new reusable hashing mechanism with its own failure analysis (Theorem 1); its smaller circuits follow from it, so the rubric routes it to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2018-PSWW-2D-CUCKOO-HASHING.selection_rationale: Lets both parties use cuckoo hashing with one shared bin per common item (§5, pp. 13-14), the protocol PSI-PAPER-2019-PSTY compares against as the previous best.

PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-AHE-THRESHOLD-PSI.label: Threshold PSI from additive HE via cardinality testing
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-AHE-THRESHOLD-PSI.lane_rationale: The paper's main protocol: a reusable decomposition into private cardinality testing and noisy polynomial addition that realizes threshold PSI without FHE; the \( \tilde O(t^{2}) \) bound follows from it.
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-AHE-THRESHOLD-PSI.selection_rationale: First threshold PSI protocols with communication depending mainly on t, per the abstract (p. 1); its cardinality test is reused by PSI-PAPER-2021-BMRR.

PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-LOWER-BOUND.label: \( \Omega(t) \) communication lower bound for threshold PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-LOWER-BOUND.lane_rationale: A communication lower bound; the rubric routes lower bounds to Foundation.
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-LOWER-BOUND.selection_rationale: Frames the communication complexity of threshold PSI and is the base of the multiparty bound of PSI-PAPER-2021-BMRR (§3, pp. 7-8).
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-LOWER-BOUND.split_rationale: Belongs to the line of communication lower bounds, separate from the protocol line of PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-AHE-THRESHOLD-PSI: it turns the disjointness-based bound of PSI-CONTRIB-2004-FNP-APPROX-LOWER-BOUND into \( \Omega(t) \) for threshold PSI, and Badrinarayanan et al. reduce their multiparty \( \Omega(nT) \) bound to it (PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-LOWER-BOUND).

PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-BATCHED-OPPRF.label: Batched OPPRF with one polynomial hint
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-BATCHED-OPPRF.lane_rationale: A reusable mechanism (one-time PPRF with correlated targets, batched hint) with its own theorems; its linear cost follows from the mechanism.
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-BATCHED-OPPRF.selection_rationale: Makes programming all bins cost linear communication (Construction 4, Theorem 5, Theorem 8, pp. 13-16).
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-BATCHED-OPPRF.split_rationale: Belongs to the OPPRF line, separate from the circuit-PSI result of PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-LINEAR-COMMUNICATION: it adapts the polynomial OPPRF of PSI-CONTRIB-2017-KMPRT-OPPRF to a one-query definition with batched hints, and VOLE-PSI replaces it in its circuit-PSI (PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-CIRCUIT-PSI).

PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-LINEAR-COMMUNICATI.label: Linear-communication circuit-PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-LINEAR-COMMUNICATI.lane_rationale: The principal claim is a named communication bound, \( O(n) \) for circuit-PSI, against \( \omega(n) \) before; the rubric routes achieving an upper cost bound to Efficiency.
PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-LINEAR-COMMUNICATI.selection_rationale: The authors call it the first circuit-based PSI with linear communication, matching the lower bound on comparisons (abstract, p. 1; §1.1, p. 4).

PSI-CONTRIB-2020-ION-DDH-INTERSECTION-SU.label: Deployed Diffie-Hellman intersection-sum with cardinality
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-ION-DDH-INTERSECTION-SU.lane_rationale: A concrete protocol realizing a new output (intersection-sum with cardinality); efficiency claims concern deployment cost rather than an asymptotic advance.
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-ION-DDH-INTERSECTION-SU.selection_rationale: A PSI variant used in industry for several years (abstract, p. 1), with proofs (Theorems 1-2, p. 6) and deployment costs (Table 2, p. 8).

PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-MALICIOUS-PAXOS-PS.label: Malicious PSI with linear communication
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-MALICIOUS-PAXOS-PS.lane_rationale: A concrete protocol answering how malicious two-party PSI with linear communication is realized, through the XOR-homomorphism of OOS outputs and a PaXoS encoding; routed to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-MALICIOUS-PAXOS-PS.selection_rationale: The authors describe it as the first concretely efficient malicious PSI with linear communication in the OT-hybrid model with a non-programmable random oracle, and the first to use cuckoo hashing for malicious PSI (abstract, p. 1; §1.1, pp. 2-3).

PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-PAXOS.label: PaXoS key-value encoding
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-PAXOS.lane_rationale: Introduces a notion: the probe-and-XOR of strings, an abstraction of input-independent binary key-value encodings with stated efficiency measures (Definition 3, p. 6; §3.4, pp. 7-8). The protocol and the concrete table are separate contributions.
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-PAXOS.selection_rationale: Defines the interface that PaXoS-PSI is written against (§4, pp. 9-11) and that the OKVS definition later generalizes.
PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-PAXOS.split_rationale: Belongs to the line of key-value-encoding definitions, separate from the protocol line of PSI-CONTRIB-2020-PRTY-MALICIOUS-PAXOS-PSI: the OKVS definition generalizes PaXoS from binary to linear encodings (PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-OKVS).

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-LOWER-BOUND.label: \( \Omega(nT) \) lower bound for multiparty threshold PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-LOWER-BOUND.lane_rationale: A communication lower bound; Foundation by the rubric.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-LOWER-BOUND.selection_rationale: Extends the two-party bound to n parties (Theorems 4.1 and 4.3, pp. 15-17).
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-LOWER-BOUND.split_rationale: Belongs to the line of communication lower bounds, separate from the protocols of PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-TAHE-THRESHOLD-PSI: it extends the bound of PSI-CONTRIB-2019-GS-LOWER-BOUND to n parties, and it is the \( \Omega(nT) \) bound that the central problem PSI-OP-005 asks protocols without FHE to match.

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-TAHE-THRESHOLD-PSI.label: \( \tilde O(nT) \) threshold PSI from threshold additive HE
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-TAHE-THRESHOLD-PSI.lane_rationale: The principal claim is a named cost improvement under a weaker assumption: \( \tilde O(T) \) instead of \( \tilde O(T^{2}) \) for two parties from additive HE, \( \tilde O(nT) \) for n parties; the Hankel test is the means.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-BMRR-TAHE-THRESHOLD-PSI.selection_rationale: Claimed by the authors to solve the Ghosh-Simkin open problem (abstract, p. 1; §1.2, p. 4); Ghosh and Simkin (2023) credit the two-party bound without FHE to their 2019 construction combined with an observation of this paper (PSI-PAPER-2023-GS, p. 4, footnote 5).

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-CONG-PATERSON-STOCKMEYE.label: \( O(\sqrt{B}) \) multiplications per sender bin
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-CONG-PATERSON-STOCKMEYE.lane_rationale: Advances a named resource, ciphertext-ciphertext multiplications of the sender, from linear to square root in the bin size; Efficiency.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-CONG-PATERSON-STOCKMEYE.selection_rationale: First claim of the abstract, \( O(\sqrt{|X|}) \) homomorphic multiplications, called a quadratic improvement over CHLR18 (abstract, p. 1; §1.2, p. 3).

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-MALICIOUS-MULTIPA.label: Malicious multiparty PSI from OPRF and OKVS
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-MALICIOUS-MULTIPA.lane_rationale: A stronger-secure protocol: an existing multiparty PSI with one modification, the random-oracle hash, shown malicious-secure; the rubric routes a stronger-secure protocol to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-MALICIOUS-MULTIPA.selection_rationale: The authors call it the most efficient malicious multiparty PSI to date (§1.3, p. 4; §7.2, p. 22).
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-MALICIOUS-MULTIPA.split_rationale: Belongs to the multiparty line, separate from the OKVS definition of PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-OKVS: it shows the augmented semi-honest protocol of Kolesnikov et al. malicious-secure with a random-oracle hash, and the protocol of Nevo, Trieu, and Yanai coincides with it at \( t = n - 1 \) and becomes cheaper for smaller t (PSI-CONTRIB-2021-NTY-MALICIOUS-THRESHOLD-CALIBRATED).

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-OKVS.label: Oblivious key-value store
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-OKVS.lane_rationale: Introduces the oblivious key-value store with linear, binary, and overfitting notions (Definitions 1-4, pp. 5-7); a definition is routed to Foundation.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-GPRTY-OKVS.selection_rationale: Defines the interface under which polynomials, garbled Bloom filters, PaXoS, and later encodings are compared and exchanged in PSI protocols (§2-3, pp. 5-9; §6, pp. 18-20).

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-NTY-MALICIOUS-THRESHOLD.label: Malicious multiparty PSI calibrated to t
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-NTY-MALICIOUS-THRESHOLD.lane_rationale: The functionality and security (malicious, \( t < n \)) match earlier protocols; the principal delta is cost that decreases with t and client communication \( O(m \kappa) \) (Table 1, p. 2; §1.2, p. 4), assembled from prior mechanisms.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-NTY-MALICIOUS-THRESHOLD.selection_rationale: The paper states that it was not known how to make earlier protocols cheaper for smaller t (§1.2, p. 4), and its protocol reduces to that of Garimella et al. only at \( t = n - 1 \).

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-CIRCUIT-PSI.label: Circuit-PSI from VOLE-based OPPRF
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-CIRCUIT-PSI.lane_rationale: A concrete circuit-PSI protocol with a new OPPRF built from the VOLE OPRF and XoPaXoS; routed to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-CIRCUIT-PSI.selection_rationale: Replaces the polynomial OPPRF of linear-communication circuit-PSI, up to 3 times faster in the authors' measurements (abstract, p. 1; Table 4, p. 29); core in circuit-based PSI.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-CIRCUIT-PSI.split_rationale: Belongs to the circuit-PSI line, separate from the VOLE-based OPRF of PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-VOLE-OPRF: it keeps the linear-communication circuit-PSI of PSI-CONTRIB-2019-PSTY-LINEAR-COMMUNICATION and replaces its polynomial OPPRF with one built from the VOLE-based OPRF and XoPaXoS.

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-VOLE-OPRF.label: Batched OPRF from vector OLE
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-VOLE-OPRF.lane_rationale: A reusable mechanism, a batched OPRF from vector OLE and an OKVS, answering how low-communication OPRF-based PSI is realized; routed to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-VOLE-OPRF.selection_rationale: Replaces OT extension with sublinear VOLE in OPRF-based PSI, reaching under 450 bits per element with malicious security for \( n = 2^{20} \) (abstract, p. 1); extended by the subfield-VOLE PSI of Raghuraman and Rindal.

PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RT-KA-TO-MALICIOUS-PSI.label: Key agreement to malicious PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RT-KA-TO-MALICIOUS-PSI.lane_rationale: A transform from key agreement to malicious PSI; the rubric routes transforms and reusable mechanisms to Construction even when they are also fast.
PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RT-KA-TO-MALICIOUS-PSI.selection_rationale: Generic transformation from two-round key agreement to malicious PSI with about one group element per item (abstract, p. 1; Figure 4, p. 11; Lemmas 5-6).

PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-SUBFIELD-VOLE.label: Subfield-VOLE PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-SUBFIELD-VOLE.lane_rationale: A named communication improvement: moving the VOLE to a subfield makes communication \( O(n\lambda + n \log n) \) instead of scaling with \( \kappa n \); routed to Efficiency.
PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-SUBFIELD-VOLE.selection_rationale: The authors call it the first PSI with communication \( O(n\lambda + n \log n) \) (abstract, p. 1); \( 180n \) bits at \( n = 2^{20} \) against \( 426n \) for VOLE-PSI (Table 2, p. 25).
PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-SUBFIELD-VOLE.split_rationale: Belongs to the VOLE line, separate from the triangulation OKVS of PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-TRIANGULATION-OKVS: it extends the VOLE-PSI protocol of PSI-CONTRIB-2021-RS-VOLE-OPRF to subfield VOLE.

PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-TRIANGULATION-OKVS.label: Triangulation OKVS
PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-TRIANGULATION-OKVS.lane_rationale: The principal delta is a named cost of the OKVS: expansion about \( 1.23n \) and encoding and decoding 13 and 64 times faster than the three-hash table, with concrete failure analysis replacing amplification; routed to Efficiency.
PSI-CONTRIB-2022-RR-TRIANGULATION-OKVS.selection_rationale: With it, OKVS-based PSI runs faster than KKRT16 in the authors' measurements (Table 2, p. 25), and the expansion is chosen directly for a target security level (§3.4, p. 21).

PSI-CONTRIB-2023-GS-PICT-COMPILER.label: Bucketing compiler for cardinality tests
PSI-CONTRIB-2023-GS-PICT-COMPILER.lane_rationale: The principal delta is a reusable transform (random partitioning, padding, and per-bucket small-threshold tests) that applies to any cardinality test; its quasilinear cost follows from it, so the rubric routes it to Construction.
PSI-CONTRIB-2023-GS-PICT-COMPILER.selection_rationale: Called the key technical contribution in the abstract (p. 1) and the main technical contribution in §1.2 (p. 2); it turns \( O(\lambda \ell \,\mathrm{poly}(t)) \) tests into \( O(\lambda^{2} \ell t \,\mathrm{polylog}\, t) \).

PSI-CONTRIB-2024-VCE-ANALYTICAL-COST-COM.label: Operation counts for semi-honest multiparty PSI
PSI-CONTRIB-2024-VCE-ANALYTICAL-COST-COM.lane_rationale: An independent comparative analysis of existing protocols' costs; it neither builds a protocol nor improves a cost.
PSI-CONTRIB-2024-VCE-ANALYTICAL-COST-COM.selection_rationale: The only new derived result of the systematization (Table 3, p. 13; Appendix B, pp. 17-18), and the basis of its conclusion that no single protocol is the state of the art (§9, p. 14).

problems.label: Malicious security
problems.question: How do protocols move from semi-honest to malicious security, and where do they stop short, by securing only one side or by not strictly enforcing a corrupt party's set size?

problems.label: Communication
problems.question: Which results bring communication down toward the size of the sets, or of the threshold in threshold PSI, and which lower bounds limit how far it can fall?

problems.label: Computation
problems.question: Which results reduce the computation of PSI, counted in public-key operations, homomorphic multiplications, circuit size, or symmetric-key work?

problems.label: Assumptions and setup
problems.question: Which protocols need only symmetric-key primitives and oblivious transfer, and which rely on public-key or homomorphic assumptions or on random oracles?

reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers the Diffie-Hellman matching protocol of Huberman, Franklin, and Hogg, which as specified outputs a match count; Freedman-Nissim-Pinkas polynomial-evaluation PSI with balanced-allocation hashing, malicious-client and malicious-server versions, and the reduction showing that PSI implies oblivious transfer; De Cristofaro-Tsudik blind-RSA PSI and linear-cost authorized PSI; and Rosulek-Trieu PSI from key agreement, malicious and semi-honest. Meadows, Hazay-Lindell, and De Cristofaro-Kim-Tsudik have no full text and no results recorded yet, and the 2016 journal version of Freedman-Nissim-Pinkas was not read.
reading_collections.excludes: Protocols whose cost is dominated by OT extension or VOLE are read under OT- and VOLE-based PSI, even though their base OTs use public-key operations. Diffie-Hellman protocols that output a cardinality or a sum are read under computing on the intersection, and homomorphic-encryption protocols for a small client set under unbalanced and labeled PSI.
reading_collections.includes: Diffie-Hellman PSI from commutative exponentiation, PSI from oblivious polynomial evaluation under homomorphic encryption, RSA blind-signature PSI, PSI from algebraic oblivious PRFs, and Bloom-filter protocols with public-key operations, as grouped under public-key-based PSI by Pinkas, Schneider, and Zohner (2018, §1.2).
reading_collections.label: Public-key-based PSI

members.reason: Commutative exponentiation of hashed items modulo a prime, the Diffie-Hellman mechanism that PSZ18 §1.2 places under public-key-based PSI; the paper gives both a matching count and, as a variation, the shared items (Appendix A, p. 85).
A cost reduction inside the polynomial-evaluation protocol; it changes neither output, model, nor set-size regime.
Malicious-secure versions of the polynomial-evaluation protocol; adversary is a facet, so the contribution stays with its mechanism.
PSI from oblivious polynomial evaluation under additively homomorphic encryption, which PSZ18 §1.2 (p. 4) lists under public-key-based PSI.

A boundary result about the two-party PSI functionality, stated among the preliminaries of the public-key protocols (§3.1, pp. 3-4); it applies to any two-party PSI protocol, not only public-key ones.
RSA blind signatures as the OPRF, the blind-RSA protocol that PSZ18 §1.2 (p. 4) lists under public-key-based PSI.
RSA-based authorized PSI and its prime-order-group PSI version, both built from per-item public-key exponentiations.
PSI from Diffie-Hellman key agreement, one exponentiation per item; RT21 itself contrasts it with OT-extension protocols (§1, pp. 1-2).
A communication improvement of semi-honest Diffie-Hellman PSI.
The variants change only the payload of the polynomial-evaluation protocol (§4.4-4.5, p. 9).
Built from the two-party polynomial-evaluation protocol under homomorphic encryption (§7, p. 15).
The baseline it measures is the one-more-DL-based protocol of De Cristofaro and Tsudik, read under public-key-based PSI.
Its masking is the commutative Diffie-Hellman technique of Meadows and of Huberman, Franklin, and Hogg, read under public-key-based PSI.

reading_collections.question: How can two parties compute the intersection of their sets with protocols built on public-key operations, and what do these protocols cost in exponentiations and communication?

reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers the batched OPRF of Kolesnikov, Kumaresan, Rosulek, and Trieu and its PSI protocol, the bit-length-independent OT-based protocol and concrete hashing parameters of the Pinkas-Schneider-Zohner journal version, Rindal-Rosulek dual execution and encode-commit, PaXoS and the garbled cuckoo table, OKVS with the three-hash table, failure amplification, and PSI from vector OLE, VOLE-PSI, and the triangulation OKVS and subfield VOLE of Raghuraman and Rindal. Dong-Chen-Wen, the Pinkas-Schneider-Zohner and Phasing conference papers, Rindal-Rosulek EUROCRYPT 2017, SpOT-light, Chase-Miao, Ghosh-Nilges, and Bui-Couteau have no full text and no results recorded yet.
reading_collections.excludes: OT extension, VOLE, and pseudorandom correlation generators as general primitives are read in the MPC atlas. Protocols that output a function of the intersection are read under computing on the intersection, protocols for a small client set under unbalanced and labeled PSI, and protocols for more than two parties under multiparty PSI.
reading_collections.includes: Protocols in the OT-based class of Pinkas, Schneider, and Zohner (2018, §1.2), including Bloom-filter protocols built on OT extension; PSI from an oblivious PRF with cuckoo hashing (Evans, Kolesnikov, and Rosulek, §3.8.1); batched and multipoint OPRFs; PaXoS and OKVS encodings; PSI from vector OLE, subfield VOLE, and OLE; and techniques that make these protocols secure against malicious parties, such as dual execution.
reading_collections.label: OT- and VOLE-based PSI

members.reason: A batched OPRF built from OT extension, which is the mechanism the OT- and OPRF-based subfield names; it is not a complete protocol and changes neither the output nor the set-size regime.
A complete semi-honest two-party PSI protocol from a batched OPRF on OT extension and cuckoo hashing, described for equal set sizes and outputting the intersection.
A malicious variant of the same OT-based paradigm, built on oblivious encodings from OT extension.
Malicious security for the OT-based paradigm of Pinkas, Schneider, and Zohner; the psi_oprf collection names dual execution among its techniques.
OT-based PSI from per-bin OPRFs on 1-out-of-N OT extension, the OT-based class of PSZ18 §1.2 itself.
Parameters for the cuckoo and simple hashing that the OT-based protocol of §5 relies on (Protocol 3, p. 22).
The concrete PaXoS data structure used by PaXoS-PSI and later as the solver of VOLE-PSI.
Two-party PSI from OT extension and a PaXoS encoding, outputting the intersection for balanced sets.
A binary key-value encoding defined for OT-extension-based PSI; PaXoS and OKVS encodings are named in the OT- and VOLE-based subfield.
A security analysis of the malicious instantiation of PaXoS-PSI, a protocol of this subfield.
A binary OKVS that shrinks the table of PaXoS-PSI, a two-party OT-extension protocol.
A transform for OKVS failure probabilities, used to instantiate the OKVS of the paper's two-party PSI.
Two-party PSI from vector OLE and a linear OKVS, outputting the intersection.
The OKVS abstraction, which the subfield definition names, introduced to improve OT- and VOLE-based PSI.
An analysis of the OPRF-to-PSI transformation for two-party PSI that outputs the intersection.
A batched OPRF from vector OLE for two-party PSI, the VOLE mechanism the subfield names.
Subfield VOLE in two-party OPRF-based PSI that outputs the intersection.
An OKVS construction that improves VOLE-based two-party PSI.
Hashing items to bins is the step whose parameters PSZ18 §3 makes concrete for OT-based PSI, citing this paper's asymptotic analysis (PSZ18 §1.3, p. 5).

As a two-party primitive it extends the batched OPRF of KKRT16 that OT-based PSI reads (KMPRT §3.1, pp. 4-5); its malicious PaXoS-based instantiation and two-party uses are read under OT- and VOLE-based PSI.

Read in OT- and VOLE-based PSI for its OT-extension technique: correlated-OT precomputation for garbled-circuit and Naor-Reingold OPRF evaluation, which the authors call of independent interest (KRSSW19 §1.1, p. 2; §4.3, p. 8); its core is precomputed unbalanced PSI.
An OPPRF built from one-time OPRF instances from OT extension, read next to the batched OPRFs of OT-based PSI.
Built on the batched-OPRF PSI of Kolesnikov, Kumaresan, Rosulek, and Trieu, read under OT- and VOLE-based PSI.
Built from a malicious two-party OPRF and an OKVS; the OPRF and OKVS mechanisms are read under OT- and VOLE-based PSI.
Its OPPRF is built from the VOLE-based OPRF and the XoPaXoS encoding; those mechanisms are read under OT- and VOLE-based PSI.

reading_collections.question: How can two parties compute the intersection from oblivious transfer and its descendants, namely batched oblivious PRFs, sparse OT, PaXoS and OKVS encodings, and vector OLE, and at what communication and computation cost against semi-honest and malicious parties?

reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers Huang-Evans-Katz garbled-circuit PSI with size auditing and its measurement against custom protocols; mirror and two-dimensional cuckoo hashing for circuits (Pinkas, Schneider, Weinert, and Wieder); linear-communication circuit-PSI with batched OPPRFs and payloads (Pinkas, Schneider, Tkachenko, and Yanai) and the circuit-PSI of VOLE-PSI; intersection-sum with cardinality (Ion et al.); the Freedman-Nissim-Pinkas cardinality and threshold variants and approximation lower bound; Ghosh-Simkin threshold PSI with its lower bound; multiparty threshold PSI of Badrinarayanan, Miao, Raghuraman, and Rindal; and the bucketing compiler for cardinality tests and quasilinear multiparty threshold PSI without FHE of Ghosh and Simkin (2023). Circuit-Phasing has no full text yet.
reading_collections.excludes: Garbled circuits, GMW, and mixed-protocol frameworks as general protocols are read in the MPC atlas. Protocols that output the plain intersection are read under the subfield of their technique, even when they evaluate a circuit internally.
reading_collections.includes: Circuit-based PSI with generic secure computation, from sort-compare-shuffle circuits to cuckoo-hashing circuits with linear communication; circuit-PSI with secret-shared outputs; PSI cardinality and intersection-sum; and threshold PSI, including its communication lower bounds.
reading_collections.label: Circuit-based PSI and computing on the intersection

members.reason: A communication lower bound for approximating the intersection size, a function of the intersection; TAXONOMY.md reads such lower bounds under computing on the intersection.
The output is the intersection size or a threshold decision, which TAXONOMY.md reads under computing on the intersection regardless of technique.
Measures generic garbled-circuit PSI, the defining approach of circuit-based PSI, against custom protocols.
Computes on the intersection inside the circuit (its size and a threshold test) before deciding what to release.
A PSI protocol evaluated entirely as a generic garbled circuit; PSI-PAPER-2018-PSZ §1.2 places it under circuit-based PSI, and the subfield definition names sort-compare-shuffle circuits.
The hashing scheme for circuit-based PSI computing functions such as PSI-CAT; PSI-PAPER-2018-PSWW §1 is a basis source of the subfield.
Circuit-based PSI that computes symmetric functions of the intersection with \( \omega(n) \) comparisons.
Threshold PSI protocol; the output facet `threshold` cites this paper.
Threshold PSI upper bound; threshold output is read under computing on the intersection.
TAXONOMY reads threshold PSI, including its lower bounds, under computing on the intersection.
Introduced to make circuit-PSI linear; it is used here only to feed one comparison per bin into the circuit.
Circuit-PSI with secret outputs fed to a further circuit, the output facet `circuit` cites this paper.
Brings associated data of intersecting items into the circuit, for functions such as sums over the intersection.
Outputs intersection size and sum, not the intersection; TAXONOMY reads Ion et al. under computing on the intersection although the technique is Diffie-Hellman.
Outputs intersection size and sum over a hidden intersection.
Per LITERATURE_COVERAGE.md and TAXONOMY.md, a multi-party threshold result is core under the subfield of its principal claim; the principal claim concerns the threshold condition.
A communication lower bound in terms of the threshold T; threshold PSI lower bounds are read under computing on the intersection (TAXONOMY.md).
Threshold PSI from threshold additive HE, claimed to settle the two-party question of PSI-PAPER-2019-GS; principal claim concerns the threshold.
Threshold PSI with communication sublinear in the set size; principal claim concerns the threshold (the psi_multiparty excludes note).
The output is secret shares for a further computation (circuit-PSI), which places the contribution in circuit-based PSI by output.
Multi-party threshold PSI whose principal claim concerns the dependence on the threshold t, placed like PSI-PAPER-2021-BMRR per LITERATURE_COVERAGE.md and TAXONOMY.md.
A compiler for intersection cardinality tests, the threshold-PSI building block; threshold PSI is read under computing on the intersection (TAXONOMY.md).
The protocol as specified outputs the number of matches to both parties, not the matches (Appendix A, step 5, p. 85), so it is also read as an early intersection-cardinality protocol.
The same parameters size the pairwise-comparison circuit for circuit-based PSI (§4.2, pp. 19-20; Table 11, p. 30).
The circuit-PSI of the same paper builds its OPPRF on this OPRF; that use is read under circuit-based PSI.
Also applied, in a doubly oblivious form, to the circuit-PSI of VOLE-PSI (Table 2, p. 25); that use is read under circuit-based PSI.

reading_collections.question: How can parties learn a function of the intersection, such as its size, a sum over it, whether it is large enough, or secret shares for a further computation, without learning the intersection itself, and how much communication does this require?

reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers Chen-Laine-Rindal PSI from leveled FHE; Chen-Huang-Laine-Rindal OPRF preprocessing against a malicious receiver, long items, labeled PSI, and malicious-sender security up to bounded leakage; Kales et al. precomputed OPRF-based contact discovery on phones; and the evaluation, encoding, and communication optimizations of Cong et al. Kiss et al. 2017 and Resende-Aranha have no cards, and PSI with computation (Chen-Huang-Laine-Rindal §6) is not recorded.
reading_collections.excludes: Keyword PIR, SealPIR, and batch codes are read in the PIR atlas, and BFV, batching, and Paillier in the HE atlas. Balanced protocols that are only evaluated on unequal sets, as in Pinkas, Schneider, and Zohner (2018, §6.2.3), are read under the subfield of their technique.
reading_collections.includes: PSI from fully homomorphic encryption for a small client set, labeled PSI, OPRF preprocessing against malicious parties in this setting, and private contact discovery.
reading_collections.label: Unbalanced and labeled PSI

members.reason: A complete PSI protocol designed for a small receiver set against a much larger sender set, with communication linear in the smaller and logarithmic in the larger set (CLR17 §1.4, p. 3; p. 4); this is the defining question of the unbalanced subfield.
Labeled PSI with communication sublinear in the sender's set, one of the two questions TAXONOMY assigns to this subfield (CHLR18 §5, pp. 11-12).
Security against a malicious sender for FHE-based unbalanced PSI under sublinear communication (CHLR18 §7.3, pp. 17-18; Theorem 3, p. 25).
An optimization of FHE-based unbalanced PSI that removes its item-length restriction (CHLR18 §3, pp. 7-8).
Changes the security model of FHE-based unbalanced PSI (malicious receiver) while keeping communication sublinear in the sender's set (CHLR18 §4, pp. 8-11; Theorem 1, p. 15).
Optimizes the online phase of precomputed unbalanced PSI, whose online cost depends only on the client set (KRSSW19 §3.5, p. 6; §§4.3-4.4, pp. 8-10).
Reduces the one-time transfer of the large server set in precomputed unbalanced PSI (KRSSW19 §4.1, pp. 6-7).
Reduces the base-phase cost of the garbled-circuit OPRF in precomputed unbalanced PSI for contact discovery (KRSSW19 §4.2, pp. 7-8).
An implementation result for unbalanced PSI on phones against server sets of \( 2^{20} \) to \( 2^{28} \) items (KRSSW19 §§5-6, pp. 11-14).
Makes the online communication of FHE-based unbalanced PSI nearly independent of the larger set (CMGD21 §3.1, pp. 11-12; §5.4, pp. 18-20).
Reduces the sender computation of FHE-based unbalanced and labeled PSI (CMGD21 §3.1, pp. 7-9).
Reduces receiver-to-sender communication in FHE-based unbalanced PSI (CMGD21 §3.1, pp. 10-11).
Changes the item and label encoding of FHE-based unbalanced and labeled PSI (CMGD21 §3.1, p. 7; §4.2, pp. 13-14).

reading_collections.question: How can a client with a small set intersect it with a much larger server set using communication sublinear in the server's set, retrieve labels associated with matching items, and stay secure against a malicious client or server?

reading_collections.coverage_note: Covers the Freedman-Nissim-Pinkas multiparty sketch; Kolesnikov et al. OPPRF-based protocols against semi-honest and augmented semi-honest collusion; the malicious protocol of Garimella et al.; Nevo-Trieu-Yanai protocols without collusion and calibrated to the collusion bound; and the operation counts of the Vos-Conti-Erkin systematization. Multiparty threshold PSI (Badrinarayanan et al.; Ghosh and Simkin 2023) is read as context here and as core under computing on the intersection. Kissner-Song, Hazay-Venkitasubramaniam, and the honest-majority and garbled-Bloom-filter protocols that Vos, Conti, and Erkin compare have no cards yet.
reading_collections.excludes: Server-aided, delegated, and outsourced PSI, in which a third party without input assists, are not covered. Multi-party threshold PSI is read under computing on the intersection when its principal result concerns the threshold.
reading_collections.includes: Multiparty PSI against colluding semi-honest, augmented semi-honest, or malicious parties, built from oblivious programmable PRFs, OKVS, homomorphic encryption, or secret sharing, and the systematization of Vos, Conti, and Erkin.
reading_collections.label: Multiparty PSI

members.reason: n parties compute the intersection of all their lists (§7, p. 15).
Changes the security model and cost of the multiparty protocol (Theorem 2, p. 14); it has no two-party reading.

The OPPRF is introduced as the technical core of multiparty PSI (KMPRT abstract, p. 1) and is the building block of the OPPRF-based multiparty protocols that this subfield reads (KMPRT §5; NTY Protocol 4.2).
A complete protocol for \( n > 2 \) parties against any number of colluding semi-honest parties (Theorem 1, p. 12).
More than two parties compute the intersection against malicious corruption of any subset; the subfield is fixed by the party count.
Malicious multiparty PSI with at most one corrupted party (Theorem 3.4, p. 8); its server-aided base case uses a party with input as server, so it is not in the deferred server-aided class.
Malicious multiparty PSI against \( t < n \) colluding parties whose cost depends on t (Theorem 4.5, p. 11; Table 1, p. 2).
Analyzes the costs of semi-honest collusion-resistant multiparty PSI protocols only (§7 and Table 3, pp. 12-13).
The two functionalities differ only for more than two parties, which is read under multiparty PSI.
The bound scales with the number of parties n under \( n - 1 \) corruptions, a multiparty PSI setting.
The general protocol is n-party with \( n - 1 \) collusion, read alongside multiparty PSI.
n-party protocol with \( n - 1 \) collusion in a star network, read alongside multiparty PSI.
The malicious multiparty protocol of the same paper (Appendix B) is written over an arbitrary OKVS; its multiparty use is read under multiparty PSI.
ℓ parties with all-but-one passive corruption, read alongside multiparty PSI.
Its main application is the ℓ-party test with all-but-one passive corruption, read alongside multiparty PSI.

reading_collections.question: How can more than two parties compute the intersection of their sets when up to a stated number of them collude, and how close can the cost come to that of two-party PSI?

relations.evidence_locator: FNP04 §4.2 (pp. 6-8), EUROCRYPT 2004, LNCS 3027, printed pages
relations.statement: Balanced-allocation hashing splits the client's polynomial into low-degree bin polynomials, reducing the server's exponentiations from \( O(k_C k_S) \) to \( O(k_C + k_S \ln \ln k_C) \).

relations.evidence_locator: FNP04 §4.4-4.5 (p. 9), EUROCRYPT 2004, LNCS 3027, printed pages
relations.statement: Changing the server's payload in PM-Semi-Honest yields the cardinality variant, and random payloads plus a secure circuit yield the threshold variant.

relations.evidence_locator: FNP04 §5 (pp. 9-13), EUROCRYPT 2004, LNCS 3027, printed pages
relations.statement: The malicious-client and malicious-server protocols modify PM-Semi-Honest, with balanced-allocation hashing, by cut-and-choose and by random-oracle derandomization.

relations.evidence_locator: FNP04 §7 (pp. 15-17), EUROCRYPT 2004, LNCS 3027, printed pages
relations.statement: Each client encodes its items as in the two-party protocol, and the leader evaluates all client polynomials with XOR-shared payloads.

relations.evidence_locator: FNP04 §2 (p. 2) and abstract (p. 1), EUROCRYPT 2004, LNCS 3027, printed pages
relations.statement: FNP04 contrasts its standard-model semi-honest protocol with earlier \( O(k) \)-exponentiation constructions, citing HFH99, that had been analyzed only in the random oracle model against semi-honest parties.

relations.evidence_locator: HEK12 §7.3 with footnotes 3-4 (p. 12), Figure 11 and Table 2 (p. 13), NDSS 2012 PDF dated 2011-11-28
relations.statement: HEK12 reimplement the one-more-DL-based PSI protocol of De Cristofaro and Tsudik as a client-server protocol and measure it against their garbled-circuit protocol at five security levels.
The PSI protocol runs one BaRK-OPRF instance per cuckoo bin and stash position, so each bin consumes one row of a 424-448-bit OT-extension matrix.

relations.evidence_locator: KMPRT abstract (p. 1), Table 1 (p. 3), §6.1 (pp. 14-15), IACR ePrint 2017/799, PDF dated 2017-08-24
relations.statement: Replacing the pairwise OPPRF zero-sharing phase by zero-sharing from PRF seeds lowers client communication from \( O(m t \lambda) \) to \( O(m \lambda) \) bits and the 5-party, \( 2^{20} \)-item run from 72 s to 22 s, while relaxing semi-honest to augmented semi-honest security.
KMPRT build every OPPRF from the KKRT batched OPRF, one OPRF instance per bin plus a sender hint, and inherit its related-key and leakage relaxations.

relations.evidence_locator: KMPRT §5.1-5.2 (pp. 11-12) and Figure 8 (p. 12), IACR ePrint 2017/799, PDF dated 2017-08-24
relations.statement: Conditional zero-sharing and conditional reconstruction are both realized as multi-query OPPRF instances, between every pair of parties and from each party to the leader.

relations.evidence_locator: RR17 §5.3 (pp. 8-10), §6.4 (pp. 15-16), IACR ePrint 2017/769, full version of August 9, 2017
relations.statement: Viewing the sender's encodings in dual execution as commitments, the encode-commit protocol replaces them with a standard commitment and masked decommitments.

relations.evidence_locator: CHLR18 §1.3 (p. 3) and §5.1 (pp. 11-12), IACR ePrint 2018/787, PDF dated 2018-08-27
relations.statement: CHLR18 extends the CLR17 protocol to labeled PSI: the sender additionally evaluates a label-interpolation polynomial per bin, keeping communication sublinear in the sender's set.

CHLR18 restricts what a malicious sender can do in FHE-based unbalanced PSI from forcing the intersection to be the receiver's full set, as in CLR17, to X ∩ Y ∩ leakage(Y), under an H-limited FHE assumption.
The leaky malicious-sender protocol uses labeled PSI with hash-valued labels as its only output channel and drops the intersection polynomial.

relations.evidence_locator: CHLR18 §3 (pp. 7-8) and §8.3 (p. 21), IACR ePrint 2018/787, PDF dated 2018-08-27
relations.statement: CHLR18 replaces the plaintext modulus of the item length used by CLR17 with extension-field SIMD slots, making arbitrary-length (80-bit hashed) items efficient where CLR17 was practically limited to 32 bits.

CHLR18 applies an OPRF to both sets before the CLR17 homomorphic intersection, which removes noise flooding, bin padding, and polynomial randomization and raises security from semi-honest to a malicious receiver (with privacy against a malicious sender).

relations.evidence_locator: PSWW18 §6.2 (pp. 21-23) and Table 3 (p. 23), IACR ePrint 2018/120, PDF dated 2019-01-24
relations.statement: The 2D cuckoo-hashing circuit has 1.8 to 2.8 times fewer AND gates than sort-compare-shuffle without its shuffle phase for \( n = 2^{12} \) and \( 2^{16} \), where that circuit was the previous best.

relations.evidence_locator: PSWW18 abstract (p. 1), §1.4 (p. 5), and §6.2 (pp. 21-22), IACR ePrint 2018/120, PDF dated 2019-01-24
relations.statement: Mirror cuckoo hashing reduces the comparisons of circuit-based PSI from the \( O(n \log n) \) of the sort-compare-shuffle circuit to \( \omega(n) \).

relations.evidence_locator: PSZ18 §1.2 'OT-Based PSI' (pp. 4-5), Table 1 (p. 5), §5 (p. 22), IACR ePrint 2016/930, PDF dated 2019-07-28
relations.statement: PSZ18 contrasts its fixed BCH code with KKRT16's pseudorandom code for the same OPRF role, reporting 1.10-1.15 times the communication and noting that its code admits a malicious-receiver extension that the pseudorandom code does not.
PSZ18 supplies concrete parameters for the hashing-to-bins approach that FNP04 introduced for PSI with only an asymptotic analysis.

relations.evidence_locator: GS19 abstract (p. 1) and §1 (p. 2), IACR ePrint 2019/175, PDF dated 2020-05-27
relations.statement: Earlier threshold PSI, including the FNP04 threshold decision on the intersection size, communicates at least linearly in the smaller set; GS19 reaches communication depending mainly on t.

relations.evidence_locator: GS19 §1 (p. 2), IACR ePrint 2019/175, PDF dated 2020-05-27
relations.statement: GS19 lists PSWW18 among threshold PSI solutions whose communication scales at least linearly in the smaller set, and gives protocols whose communication depends mainly on t.

relations.evidence_locator: GS19 §1 (p. 1) and §3 (pp. 7-8), IACR ePrint 2019/175, PDF dated 2020-05-27
relations.statement: Ghosh and Simkin reduce threshold PSI to PSI on padded sets and so turn the disjointness-based linear lower bound that they attribute to Freedman, Nissim, and Pinkas into an \( \Omega(t) \) bound in the threshold.

relations.evidence_locator: PSTY19 Protocol 7 (p. 16) and §7.3 (p. 24), IACR ePrint 2019/241, PDF dated 2019-02-28
relations.statement: The batched OPPRF is built in the F_OPRF-hybrid model, and its cost is estimated with the BaRK-OPRF at no more than 450 bits per evaluation.

PSTY19 adapts the polynomial OPPRF of KMPRT17 to a one-query definition that allows correlated targets and batches the hints of all bins into one polynomial of total size linear in the programmed points.

relations.evidence_locator: PSTY19 abstract (p. 1), Table 3 (p. 25), and Table 5 (p. 27), IACR ePrint 2019/241, PDF dated 2019-02-28
relations.statement: The stash-less OPPRF protocol communicates 2.6 to 12.8 times less and runs 2.8 to 5.8 times faster than the 2D cuckoo-hashing protocol, the previous best circuit-based PSI.
PSTY19 reduces the \( \omega(n) \) comparisons of the PSWW18 construction, \( s \cdot n \) of which serve a stash of size \( \omega(1) \), to \( O(n) \) comparisons and linear communication.

relations.evidence_locator: PSTY19 Protocol 9 (p. 17) and Protocol 10 (p. 20), IACR ePrint 2019/241, PDF dated 2019-02-28
relations.statement: The linear-communication circuit-PSI programs the batched OPPRF so that all of a bin's items share one target, leaving one comparison per bin in the circuit.

relations.evidence_locator: PSTY19 §6 (pp. 21-22), IACR ePrint 2019/241, PDF dated 2019-02-28
relations.statement: Payloads are injected with a second batched OPPRF whose targets differ per item, XORing the bin mask with each item's payload.

relations.evidence_locator: Ion et al. §3.1 (p. 5) and §4.2 (p. 8), IACR ePrint 2019/723, PDF dated 2020-09-05
relations.statement: Ion et al. extend the shuffled commutative-exponentiation intersection-cardinality protocol of Huberman, Franklin, and Hogg with additively homomorphic tags so that one party also learns the sum of values over the intersection.

relations.evidence_locator: Ion et al. §4.3.1 (p. 9) and §5.1 (p. 11), IACR ePrint 2019/723, PDF dated 2020-09-05
relations.statement: The random-OT protocol follows the batched-OPRF PSI of KKRT16, with its batched random OT, and adds a shuffle and re-masking of the OPRF outputs plus homomorphic tags so that the intersection stays hidden while its sum is computed.

relations.evidence_locator: PRTY20 §1.1 (pp. 2-3); Table 1 (p. 21); Table 2 (p. 24); Appendix D (pp. 34-35), IACR ePrint 2020/193, PDF dated 2020-02-16
relations.statement: PaXoS-PSI improves on the communication of Rindal-Rosulek dual-execution malicious PSI from \( O(\kappa n \log n) \) to \( O(\kappa n) \), replacing hashing into small bins with a PaXoS encoding over OOS; for \( 2^{20} \) items it reports 202.04 MB against 22,183 MB for the dual-execution variant with 64-bit items and 1,322 MB for the encode-commit variant.

relations.evidence_locator: BMRR §1.1 (p. 2) and §2.3 (p. 6), IACR ePrint 2020/600, PDF dated 2021-02-25
relations.statement: BMRR generalize the two-party threshold PSI functionality of GS19 to two multiparty functionalities that coincide for two parties.

relations.evidence_locator: BMRR Theorems 4.1 and 4.3 with proofs (pp. 15-17), IACR ePrint 2020/600, PDF dated 2021-02-25
relations.statement: BMRR derive the per-party \( \Omega(T) \) and total \( \Omega(nT) \) bounds for multiparty threshold PSI by reducing from the two-party \( \Omega(T) \) bound of GS19.

relations.evidence_locator: BMRR abstract (p. 1), §1.2 (p. 4), §3.3-3.4 (pp. 12-14), Imported Theorem 6.4 (p. 27), IACR ePrint 2020/600, PDF dated 2021-02-25
relations.statement: BMRR keep the monomial encoding, Hankel sparsity test, and noisy-polynomial intersection step of GS19 and replace the general singularity test with a Hankel-specific half-GCD test, lowering two-party communication from \( \tilde O(T^{2}) \) to \( \tilde O(T) \) without FHE.

relations.evidence_locator: BMRR §3.1 (pp. 11-12) and §5.1 (p. 17), IACR ePrint 2020/600, PDF dated 2021-02-25
relations.statement: BMRR start from the two-party FHE protocol of GS19 and generalize it to n parties under threshold FHE, adding random linear factors against unexpected degree reduction.

CMGD21 lowers the number of encrypted query powers from \( O(\log B) \), as with CLR17 windowing, to \( O(1) \) using depth-free Frobenius operations, reducing communication from \( \tilde O(2^{C} C^{2}) \) to \( \tilde O(C^{2}) \) with \( C = \log \log |X| \).

relations.evidence_locator: CMGD21 §1.2 (p. 3) and §3.1 (pp. 7-8), IACR ePrint 2021/1116, PDF dated 2021-11-14
relations.statement: CMGD21 replaces computing all powers up to the partition size, as in the CLR17 framework retained by CHLR18, with Paterson-Stockmeyer evaluation, reducing non-scalar multiplications per bin from linear to \( O(\sqrt{B}) \).

relations.evidence_locator: CMGD21 §1.2 (p. 3) and §3.1 (pp. 9-10), IACR ePrint 2021/1116, PDF dated 2021-11-14
relations.statement: CMGD21 replaces the windowing introduced by CLR17 with extremal postage-stamp bases, sending fewer encrypted powers for the same depth.
CMGD21 builds its labeled mode on the CHLR18 approach of encrypting labels under part of the OPRF output and interpolating the encrypted labels, adapting it to prime-field chunks.

relations.evidence_locator: CMGD21 §1.2 (p. 3) and §3.1 (p. 7), IACR ePrint 2021/1116, PDF dated 2021-11-14
relations.statement: CMGD21 replaces the extension-field SIMD slots that CHLR18 used for arbitrary-length items with items split over prime-field slots.

relations.evidence_locator: CMGD21 §3 (p. 6) and §3.1 (p. 7), IACR ePrint 2021/1116, PDF dated 2021-11-14
relations.statement: Prime-field slots are safe only because CMGD21 makes the CHLR18 OPRF step mandatory: partial matches of OPRF outputs reveal nothing about the sender's items.

relations.evidence_locator: GPRTY21 §3 (p. 9); §4.1 (pp. 9-11); Figure 1 (p. 8); Table 2 (p. 29), IACR ePrint 2021/883, PDF dated 2021-11-30
relations.statement: The three-hash table generalizes the PaXoS garbled cuckoo table from two to three hash functions, keeping its \( L \| R \) treatment of the 2-core, and reduces the main table from about \( 2.4n \) to \( 1.3n \) positions.
Used as the binary OKVS of PaXoS-PSI, the three-hash table reduces the malicious protocol's communication 1.61 times for \( 2^{20} \) items, because \( 1.3n \) OTs replace \( 2.4n \).
GPRTY21 responds to the practice, as in PSZ18, of extrapolating cuckoo-hashing failure probabilities from large experiments, by amplifying an empirically validated OKVS failure rate instead.

relations.evidence_locator: GPRTY21 §7.1 (pp. 20-21); Figure 3 (p. 22), IACR ePrint 2021/883, PDF dated 2021-11-30
relations.statement: The generalized protocol adapts PaXoS-PSI to any linear OKVS by replacing the OOS correlation with vector OLE, which removes the error-correcting code.

relations.evidence_locator: GPRTY21 §6.2 (p. 19), IACR ePrint 2021/883, PDF dated 2021-11-30
relations.statement: GPRTY21 observes that the VOLE-PSI OPRF combines vector OLE with PaXoS and that any OKVS can replace PaXoS there; its own vector-OLE protocol is derived from PaXoS-PSI.

relations.evidence_locator: GPRTY21 §7.2 (pp. 21-22); Appendix B.2 (p. 30); Appendix B.6 (pp. 36-37), IACR ePrint 2021/883, PDF dated 2021-11-30
relations.statement: GPRTY21 shows that this protocol, with each OPRF output hashed together with the item by a random oracle and written over any OKVS, is secure against malicious adversaries.
The OKVS definition generalizes PaXoS from binary to linear and other key-value encodings and makes obliviousness explicit; a binary OKVS is a PaXoS.

relations.evidence_locator: GPRTY21 §2.4, Definition 4 and Lemma 5 (pp. 6-7), IACR ePrint 2021/883, PDF dated 2021-11-30
relations.statement: GPRTY21 observes that the PaXoS bound on encodable random-oracle values uses only correctness, restates it for any key-value store, and formalizes it as the (n, n')-overfitting game.

relations.evidence_locator: NTY §2.0.4 (p. 5), Protocols 3.1 and 3.3 (pp. 6, 8), proof of Theorem 3.2 (p. 7), IACR ePrint 2021/1221, PDF dated 2021-09-17
relations.statement: P1 and the other senders encode their items with PRF values in OKVSs, whose obliviousness the simulation uses to replace them with random encodings.

relations.evidence_locator: NTY §2.0.5 (p. 5), §4.1 and Protocol 4.2 (p. 10), Protocol C.1 (p. 14), IACR ePrint 2021/1221, PDF dated 2021-09-17
relations.statement: ZeroXOR masks each OPPRF-programmed value with the unconditional zero-sharing of KMPRT, which NTY restate as a functionality and protocol, and uses it against a malicious adversary.

relations.evidence_locator: NTY §2 (pp. 4-5), Protocol 4.2 (p. 10), §5 (p. 11), IACR ePrint 2021/1221, PDF dated 2021-09-17
relations.statement: NTY take the OPPRF definitions almost verbatim from KMPRT and run an OPPRF from each of t parties to P_n inside ZeroXOR.

relations.evidence_locator: NTY §5.1 and Tables 3-4 (pp. 11-12), IACR ePrint 2021/1221, PDF dated 2021-09-17
relations.statement: NTY report 10-23 times lower client running time and 1.2-8.5 times lower total running time than the semi-honest KMPRT protocol, while being maliciously secure.

relations.evidence_locator: NTY §1.1.1 (p. 2), §2.0.3 (p. 5), Appendix B (p. 14), IACR ePrint 2021/1221, PDF dated 2021-09-17
relations.statement: NTY instantiate the OPPRF of ZeroXOR with the maliciously secure PaXoS-based OPPRF, which resists a sender that programs a point in only some cuckoo bins.

At \( t = n - 1 \) the NTY protocol coincides with that of Garimella et al. up to the OKVS instantiation, with the same performance; for smaller t it removes clients from the zero test and becomes cheaper.

relations.evidence_locator: NTY §2.0.4 (p. 5), Protocol 4.4 (p. 10), §5 (p. 11), IACR ePrint 2021/1221, PDF dated 2021-09-17
relations.statement: Each client sends the pivot a single OKVS encoding its items instead of running pairwise OPPRFs, using the OKVS definition of Garimella et al. and PaXoS as the instance they prove oblivious.
VOLE-PSI replaces the polynomial-interpolation OPPRF of PSTY19 with an OPPRF built from the VOLE-based OPRF and a XoPaXoS encoding of the sender's corrections.

VOLE-PSI's circuit-PSI keeps the PSTY19 protocol and replaces its polynomial-based OPPRF with one built from the VOLE OPRF and XoPaXoS; for \( 2^{20} \) items it runs in 23.3 s against 72.0 s at 5 Gbps with IKNP-based GMW.

relations.evidence_locator: RS21 §2 (pp. 10-11); Figure 1 (p. 7); Theorem 5.1 (pp. 21-22), IACR ePrint 2021/266, PDF dated 2024-08-08
relations.statement: XoPaXoS modifies the PaXoS solver to sample its free positions at random, so that the encoding is uniform for uniform values, as the OPPRF requires.

relations.evidence_locator: RS21 §5 (p. 21); Figure 8 (p. 38), IACR ePrint 2021/266, PDF dated 2024-08-08
relations.statement: The OPPRF of the circuit-PSI is built on the VOLE-based OPRF of the same paper.
VOLE-PSI shows that the \( 2\kappa \)-bit sender values required by the PaXoS-PSI analysis can be reduced to κ bits by extracting only non-colliding OPRF queries.
The VOLE-based OPRF encodes the receiver's set with the PaXoS solver with \( 2.4n \) main positions.

VOLE-PSI builds on PaXoS-PSI but replaces OT extension with sublinear VOLE, sending κ rather than about \( 5\kappa \) bits per encoding position with malicious security; for \( 2^{20} \) items it reports 57.86 MB against 247.6 MB.

relations.evidence_locator: RS21 §2, Eq. (1) and Conjecture 2.1 (pp. 11-12); Lemma 3.3 (p. 18), IACR ePrint 2021/266, PDF dated 2024-08-08
relations.statement: The malicious-receiver proof of the VOLE-based OPRF uses the PaXoS bound to limit the receiver's effective set to \( O(n) \), and conjectures a tighter bound of m.

relations.evidence_locator: RT21 §1 (p. 2), §1.2 (pp. 5-6), Table 1 (p. 4), IACR ePrint 2021/1159, version of October 17, 2021
relations.statement: RT21's semi-honest variants send one key-agreement message, one field element per receiver item, and one short key per sender item, against the classic Diffie-Hellman protocol's group element per item in both directions, which RT21 names as the protocol it improves.

relations.evidence_locator: RT21 abstract (p. 1), §1 (p. 2), §1.2 (pp. 5-6), IACR ePrint 2021/1159, version of October 17, 2021
relations.statement: RT21 present their malicious protocol as an improvement of the classic Diffie-Hellman protocol of Huberman, Franklin, and Hogg: \( n + 1 \) group elements plus n hashes against \( 2n \) group elements plus n hashes, while security rises from semi-honest to malicious.

relations.evidence_locator: RT21 Appendix A.1 (pp. 23-24) and A.2 (p. 26), IACR ePrint 2021/1159, version of October 17, 2021
relations.statement: The semi-honest variants keep the malicious protocol's structure and drop the random oracles H1 and H2 used only for extraction, shortening the sender's keys; variant 2 also drops the ideal permutation.

Raghuraman and Rindal extend the VOLE-PSI protocol to subfield VOLE, so that the OKVS lives in a base field of about \( \lambda + \log(n_x n_y) \) bits; for \( 2^{20} \) items they report \( 180n \) bits against \( 426n \).

relations.evidence_locator: RR22 abstract (p. 1); §1 (p. 2); Table 2 (p. 25), IACR ePrint 2022/320, PDF dated 2022-11-02
relations.statement: With the new OKVS, RR22's fast semi-honest PSI runs in 369 ms for \( 2^{20} \) items against 2,073 ms for KKRT16 on the same laptop.

relations.evidence_locator: RR22 §1 (p. 3); §5.1 and Table 1 (pp. 23-25), IACR ePrint 2022/320, PDF dated 2022-11-02
relations.statement: The triangulation OKVS keeps weight-3 rows but replaces the three-hash table's wholesale 2-core solving and two traversals by greedy triangulation with a few dense columns; encoding \( 2^{20} \) items is 13 times faster and the expansion is 1.23 rather than 1.3.

relations.evidence_locator: RR22 §5.1 (p. 24), IACR ePrint 2022/320, PDF dated 2022-11-02
relations.statement: Raghuraman and Rindal argue that the empirical 2-core bound behind the star instantiation is in error, likely costing a few bits (λ about 27 rather than 29), and replace amplification by direct parameter selection at expansion 1.23 to 1.28 instead of 1.32.

relations.evidence_locator: RR22 §1 (p. 2); Appendix A.1-A.2, Definitions 1-3 and Theorems 1-2 (pp. 30-31), IACR ePrint 2022/320, PDF dated 2022-11-02
relations.statement: The triangulation construction is a linear OKVS in the sense of the OKVS abstraction, and RR22 adds a doubly oblivious variant for circuit PSI.

relations.evidence_locator: GS23 abstract (p. 1), §1 (p. 1), §1.2 (p. 2), and Corollary 6 (p. 16), IACR ePrint 2023/919, PDF dated 2023-06-12
relations.statement: GS23 reuses the GS19 step for computing a large intersection and replaces the quadratic dependence on t of cardinality testing from additive HE by a quasilinear one, now for ℓ parties.

relations.evidence_locator: GS23 §1 (pp. 1-2), IACR ePrint 2023/919, PDF dated 2023-06-12
relations.statement: GS23 note that the BMRR \( \tilde O(\lambda \ell t) \) protocol without FHE is equivalent to two-party threshold PSI for \( \ell = 2 \) but for \( \ell > 2 \) requires fewer than t distinct elements outside the intersection among all sets, a condition GS23's large-intersection protocol does not impose.

relations.evidence_locator: GS23 §1 (pp. 1-2) and Corollary 6 (p. 16), IACR ePrint 2023/919, PDF dated 2023-06-12
relations.statement: For the large-intersection condition, where BMRR reach \( O(nT) \) only from threshold FHE, GS23 reach \( O(\lambda^{2} \ell t \,\mathrm{polylog}\, t) \) from oblivious transfer or additively homomorphic encryption, at an extra security-parameter and polylog factor.

GS23 follows the GS19 split into a cardinality test and an intersection step, and instantiates the inner two-party test of its compiler with the GS19 cardinality test, adapted to secret-shared output and run at logarithmic thresholds.

relations.evidence_locator: GS23 §1.3, paper outline paragraph, and footnote 5 (p. 4), IACR ePrint 2023/919, PDF dated 2023-06-12
relations.statement: GS23 credit the two-party \( O(\lambda t \,\mathrm{polylog}\, t) \) bound without FHE to the GS19 construction combined with an observation of BMRR, and say their own two-party protocol does not improve on it asymptotically.

relations.evidence_locator: VCE Table 3 (p. 13) and Appendix B.2 (p. 18), IACR ePrint 2023/1777, PDF dated 2023-11-16
relations.statement: VCE count \( 7(n - 1)k \) OTs at the leader, \( 3.5(n - 1)k \) per assistant, and \( 3.5(n + 1)(n - 1)k \) in total for the KMPRT protocol, from its OPPRF calls at 3.5 OTs each.

relations.evidence_locator: VCE §5.3.3 (pp. 11-12), Table 3 (p. 13), Appendix B.2 (p. 18), IACR ePrint 2023/1777, PDF dated 2023-11-16
relations.statement: VCE count tk OPPRFs at the leader and k per assistant for the ZeroXOR step of NTY, 3.5tk OTs in total, and describe it as outperforming the protocols of Kolesnikov et al., Ben-Efraim et al., and Chandran et al.

comparison_groups.label: Semi-honest two-party protocols
comparison_groups.reason: Each row is proved secure against semi-honest parties; rows differ in security model (standard model for Freedman-Nissim-Pinkas, random oracle or ideal permutation for the others) and in technique, which the comparison shows.

comparison_groups.label: Malicious two-party protocols
comparison_groups.reason: Each row resists a malicious party: the Freedman-Nissim-Pinkas rows only a malicious client (standard model) or only a malicious server (random oracle model), Rosulek-Trieu a malicious sender or receiver; the adversary scope stays visible.

comparison_groups.label: Protocols without a stated adversary model
comparison_groups.reason: Huberman, Franklin, and Hogg state no adversary model or proof; the row outputs a match count to both parties, as specified.

subfield_views.comparison_note: Rows are compared as published; differences in adversary, security model, and output are shown, not normalized. The authorized PSI of De Cristofaro and Tsudik has no row.
subfield_views.problem_note: Public-key-based protocols are rows of the goal of efficient malicious two-party PSI; its concrete problem, malicious PSI deployable for contact discovery, is drawn under unbalanced PSI and referenced here. Malicious-model versions of the linear-cost protocols of De Cristofaro and Tsudik are asked for by that paper alone, and the slack in the set size of a corrupt receiver in Rosulek and Trieu's malicious protocol is shared with the OT- and VOLE-based protocols.

comparison_groups.label: Semi-honest two-party protocols
comparison_groups.reason: Each row is a complete semi-honest two-party protocol that outputs the intersection, described and measured for equal set sizes; rows differ in OPRF, encoding, and security model.

comparison_groups.label: Malicious two-party protocols
comparison_groups.reason: Each row resists malicious parties with output to one party; rows differ in security model, in how strictly a corrupt party's set size is enforced, and in whether costs were measured.

subfield_views.comparison_note: Rows are compared as published; measurements come from different machines, networks, and item lengths and are not ranked across papers.
subfield_views.problem_note: The malicious OT- and VOLE-based protocols are the rows of the goal of efficient malicious two-party PSI that resist both parties, but they have only been run on balanced sets; its concrete problem, malicious PSI deployable for contact discovery, is drawn under unbalanced PSI and referenced here. The fastest malicious protocols bound a corrupt party's set only up to a constant factor, and conjectures about overfitting polynomials and key-value stores would tighten the bound without a common target; concrete failure probabilities of cuckoo hashing and cuckoo-style key-value stores at the parameters in use rest on experiments and extrapolation; and output to both parties under malicious security is named as a challenge without an efficiency target.

comparison_groups.label: Garbled-circuit PSI
comparison_groups.reason: Each row evaluates the whole PSI computation as a semi-honest Yao garbled circuit and outputs the intersection; rows differ in circuit design and cost.

comparison_groups.label: Circuit-PSI
comparison_groups.reason: Each row is semi-honest two-party PSI whose per-bin results are secret-shared into a further circuit; rows differ in hashing, OPPRF, and the generic protocol that evaluates the circuit.

comparison_groups.label: PSI cardinality and intersection-sum
comparison_groups.reason: Each row outputs the intersection size without the intersection; the Ion et al. rows also output a sum of associated values.

comparison_groups.label: Two-party threshold PSI
comparison_groups.reason: Each row reveals the intersection only when the sets differ in few items, with communication governed by the threshold; rows differ in assumption (FHE, additively homomorphic encryption, or oblivious transfer) and in the factors hidden by the bounds.

comparison_groups.label: Multiparty threshold PSI
comparison_groups.reason: Each row is multiparty threshold PSI against semi-honest corruption of all but one party; rows differ in the threshold condition (the two functionalities of Badrinarayanan et al., or the large-intersection condition of Ghosh and Simkin 2023) and in assumption.

subfield_views.comparison_note: Rows are compared as published; outputs differ by group (intersection, secret shares, cardinality and sum, threshold), and lower bounds are read on the map, not as rows.
subfield_views.problem_note: One key problem, the last open rung of the goal of multiparty threshold PSI at optimal communication without FHE: multiparty threshold PSI whose communication matches the known lower bound without fully homomorphic encryption. Malicious security for hashing-based circuit-PSI, named open by three papers here, is claimed by protocols published after 2022 that this atlas does not yet cover, so it is not drawn as open; concretely efficient threshold PSI is named as a goal without a threshold.

comparison_groups.label: Unbalanced PSI based on FHE
comparison_groups.reason: Each row has the sender evaluate the intersection homomorphically on the receiver's encrypted set, with communication sublinear in the sender's set; rows differ in adversary and implementation.

comparison_groups.label: Labeled PSI
comparison_groups.reason: Each row returns the labels the sender associates with matching items, from FHE.

comparison_groups.label: Unbalanced PSI based on OPRF
comparison_groups.reason: Each row sends an OPRF-encrypted filter of the server set once and evaluates the OPRF online, so setup communication is linear in the server set; rows differ in the OPRF.

subfield_views.comparison_note: Rows are compared as published; FHE-based and OPRF-based rows place communication in different phases, which the comparison shows.
subfield_views.problem_note: Two key problems of the goal of efficient malicious two-party PSI: its asymptotic rung, full security against a malicious sender while communication stays sublinear in the sender's set, and its concrete rung, malicious PSI that meets the contact-discovery requirements Signal's developers stated (\( 10^{9} \) users, address books of up to 10,000 contacts, lookups under 2 s).

comparison_groups.label: Semi-honest and augmented semi-honest protocols
comparison_groups.reason: Each row is secure against semi-honest or augmented semi-honest parties; rows differ in collusion bound, party count, and model, which the comparison shows.

comparison_groups.label: Malicious protocols
comparison_groups.reason: Each row resists malicious parties with output to one party; the corruption threshold differs, from at most one corrupted party to any strict subset.

subfield_views.comparison_note: Rows are compared as published; collusion bound, output recipients, and party count are shown, not normalized.
subfield_views.problem_note: No question about multiparty PSI is yet named open in a precise form. The key problem on multiparty threshold PSI without fully homomorphic encryption is drawn under circuit-based PSI and referenced here. Collusion-resistant multiparty PSI close to two-party cost is named open by one survey, strict enforcement of corrupt parties' set sizes by one paper, and malicious protocols with output to every party are named as a challenge without an efficiency target.

threads.description: Commutative Diffie-Hellman, oblivious polynomial evaluation under homomorphic encryption, blind-RSA, and key-agreement protocols, the public-key-based class of Pinkas, Schneider, and Zohner.
threads.label: Public-key PSI

threads.description: Oblivious PRFs evaluated with OT extension or precomputed OTs: the Pinkas-Schneider-Zohner paradigm, the batched OPRF of Kolesnikov et al., dual execution, and OPRF-based unbalanced PSI with precomputation.
threads.label: OT extension and OPRFs

threads.description: Key-value encodings (PaXoS, garbled cuckoo tables, OKVS) and the vector-OLE OPRFs built on them, for semi-honest and malicious two-party PSI.
threads.label: PaXoS, OKVS, and VOLE

threads.description: Generic secure computation of PSI and of functions of the intersection, from sort-compare-shuffle circuits to hashing-based circuits and OPPRF-based circuit-PSI.
threads.label: Circuit-based PSI

threads.description: Threshold PSI and its communication bounds, from the disjointness-based lower bound through Ghosh-Simkin to multiparty threshold PSI.
threads.label: Threshold PSI

threads.description: Unbalanced and labeled PSI in which the sender evaluates the intersection homomorphically on the receiver's encrypted set, with communication sublinear in the larger set.
threads.label: FHE-based unbalanced PSI

threads.description: Zero-sharing among more than two parties delivered through oblivious programmable PRFs or OKVS encodings, and analyses of these protocols.
threads.label: Multiparty PSI from OPPRF and OKVS
